description_full: U.S. Physical Therapy, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates and manages outpatient physical therapy clinics. It operates through two segments, Physical Therapy Operations and Industrial Injury Prevention Services. The company provides pre-and post-operative care and treatment for orthopedic-related disorders, sports-related injuries, preventative care, rehabilitation of injured workers, and neurological-related injuries. It offers industrial injury prevention services, including onsite injury prevention and rehabilitation, performance optimization, post-offer employment testing, functional capacity evaluations, and ergonomic assessments through physical therapists and specialized certified athletic trainers for Fortune 500 companies, and other clients comprising insurers and their contractors. U.S. Physical Therapy, Inc. was founded in 1990 and is based in Houston, Texas.

Each employee generates $13K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $2K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 15× revenue per employee (reasonable relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (4/10).
financial_summary: U.S. Physical Therapy, Inc. is a small-cap healthcare business with a $1.5B market cap on $781M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +9% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 10% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 23% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $61M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.90× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 9.2×.
Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.6% of the shares.
